spec.source_note: Cases are transcribed from the vendored OpenDocument v1.4 Part 4 formula standard; expected values are scalar semantics, not Excel compatibility assumptions.

included: constant Number, Text, Logical, and Error operands
implicit scalar conversions explicitly required by §§6.3.1, 6.3.5, and 6.3.14
standard arithmetic, comparison, concatenation, unary, percentage, and error propagation operators
excluded_from_normative_values: worksheet references and implied intersection, which require a formula-cell context
numeric overflow, precision, and Number subtypes where the standard permits implementation limits
text-to-Number conversion, case settings, collation, and distinct-Logical representation; those cases are listed separately

normative_cases.why: The addition operator adds two Number operands and returns a Number.
The subtraction operator subtracts the second Number from the first.
The multiplication operator multiplies two Number operands.
The division operator divides the first Number by the second.

expected.error: an Error value; the standard does not select a specific error code

normative_cases.why: Division by zero is an explicit operator constraint and returns an Error.
Exponentiation returns POWER(Left, Right), so 2 raised to 3 is 8.
The operator table specifies left associativity: (2^3)^2, rather than a right-associated power.
Parentheses make the negative exponent explicit; the power operation computes 2 raised to -1.
Prefix plus returns its argument without conversion or numeric alteration.
Prefix plus accepts Any and performs no conversion on a Text operand.
Prefix minus computes 0 minus its Number argument.
The standard explicitly gives prefix minus higher precedence than power, yielding (-2)^2.
Parentheses override the prefix/power precedence relationship, so the power is evaluated before negation.
The percentage postfix operator computes its Number operand divided by 100.
The parenthesized addition produces 5, then percentage divides that result by 100.
Multiplication has higher precedence than addition.
The operator table specifies left associativity: (8-3)-2.
Division and multiplication share precedence and associate left: (8/2)*2.
The ampersand operator concatenates two Text values.
The empty Text value contributes no characters to concatenation.
Conversion to Text transforms each Number without whitespace before the required concatenation.
Conversion to Text spells logical values exactly TRUE and FALSE, independent of their concrete representation.
Conversion to Number maps TRUE to 1 before addition.
Conversion to Number maps FALSE to 0 before addition.
Two equal Number values compare equal and produce TRUE.
Two unequal Number values compare unequal and produce FALSE.
Ordered comparison of two Numbers uses numeric order.
A Number compares less than or equal to itself.
Ordered comparison of two Numbers uses numeric order.
A Number compares greater than or equal to itself.
Identical Text values match and compare equal.
Distinct same-case Text values do not match.
The equality operator returns FALSE when the operand types differ; it does not apply text-to-number conversion.
Not-equal is the negation of equality when neither operand is an Error.
Identical Number values compare equal, so not-equal returns FALSE.
Two identical Logical values compare equal regardless of whether the evaluator stores them as a distinct type or as logical Numbers.
TRUE and FALSE are distinct logical values.
Not-equal negates the comparison of the distinct TRUE and FALSE values.
When both operands are Logical, ordered comparison converts them to Number; 1 is greater than 0.
Logical ordered comparison uses Number conversion, so 0 is less than or equal to 1.
#N/A is a distinct OpenFormula Error value.
An operator receiving an Error returns an input Error unless specifically defined otherwise.
The subtraction operator has no exception to the general Error propagation rule.
The multiplication operator propagates its Error operand.
Power receives an Error operand and propagates it before numeric exponentiation.
The not-equal operator explicitly returns an Error when either operand is an Error.
Ordered comparison cannot convert an Error to a scalar comparison operand and therefore propagates it.
The ampersand operator has no Error-suppression exception, so the input Error is retained.

expected.error: an Error value; equality cannot determine identity of constant Error values

normative_cases.why: The standard forbids using equality against a constant Error to determine whether two Error values are the same.

implementation_defined_cases.why: The infix POWER constraint permits evaluators to evaluate 0^0, and the POWER function explicitly makes the result implementation-defined: it shall be 0, 1, or an Error. This case must not be treated as a universal Error requirement.

allowed_results.condition: text is converted to the Number 2

host_dependent_cases.why: Text-to-Number conversion is implementation-defined and may depend on locale; the evaluator may parse, use 0, or return Error.

allowed_results.condition: locale treats comma as decimal separator and conversion succeeds
locale treats comma as a grouping separator and conversion succeeds

host_dependent_cases.why: The standard calls out locale-dependent group and decimal separators; this must not be fixed to an Excel-style result.

expected.condition: TRUE when HOST-CASE-SENSITIVE is false; FALSE when it is true

host_dependent_cases.why: Case sensitivity is a host calculation setting, so the standard does not select one result for case-only Text differences.

expected.condition: depends on HOST-CASE-SENSITIVE and host text ordering

host_dependent_cases.why: Ordered Text comparison is subject to host case sensitivity and collation behavior; no Excel collation is assumed.
The type section leaves Unicode normalization behavior implementation-defined, and ordered Text comparison does not prescribe a universal collation.

expected.condition: FALSE for a distinct Logical type; TRUE when Logical is represented by Number 1

host_dependent_cases.why: The standard explicitly permits distinct Logical values or Number representations and gives both equality outcomes.

expected.condition: the standard permits TRUE, FALSE, or Error when ordered-comparison operand types differ

host_dependent_cases.why: Ordered comparison leaves the result implementation-defined when operand types differ; this is not a text-to-number test.
The expression deliberately exposes locale/text conversion policy instead of treating the word TRUE as a universally numeric literal.
